sources.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3 (Living Reviews 22:3, DOI 10.1007/s41114-019-0019-x), 202 PDF pages
sources.locator: Section 1.11 printed pp. 15-16 (causal and chronological relations); section 1.12 printed pp. 17-18 with Definition 1.22 and Theorem 1.23 printed p. 19 (isotone, time and temporal functions); section 4.4 printed pp. 137-141 (stable causality and time functions); Definition 2.16 printed p. 33 and Lemma 2.17 printed pp. 33-34 (inextendibility and unbounded h-arclength domains); Theorem 2.12 printed pp. 32-33 (locally Lipschitz parametrisation of continuous causal curves); Definition 2.19 printed p. 34 and Definition 2.95 printed p. 63 with sections 2.14-2.15 printed pp. 59-66 (achronal and acausal sets); section 2.11 printed pp. 45-49 (limit curve theorems); sections 3.1-3.3 printed pp. 83-103 with Definition 3.14 printed p. 87 and Definition 3.35 printed p. 95 (domains of dependence, Cauchy horizons, Cauchy hypersurfaces); Definition 1.34 printed p. 24 and sections 4.2-4.5 printed pp. 111-148 with Definition 4.117 printed p. 146 and Theorem 4.119 printed p. 147 (causal ladder, global hyperbolicity); sections 6.2-6.3 printed pp. 161-169 (Weingarten map, Riccati and Raychaudhuri equations)

contents.name: Sections 1.11 and 2.5 printed pp. 15-16 and 32-33: causal and chronological relations over continuous causal curves, locally Lipschitz parametrisation (Theorem 2.12), Definition 2.16 inextendibility printed p. 33
contents.support: The curve class, the relations and the convergence convention of Definition 2.16 are restated with the absolutely continuous parametrization and proved equivalent to extendibility where used in lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension.

contents.name: Section 1.1 printed pp. 3-6 and section 1.11 printed pp. 15-16: Minkowski spacetime as the basic model, the timelike/null/spacelike classification and the chronological and causal relations in inertial coordinates
contents.support: The local flat model of the page fixes R^4 with the constant Lorentz form diag(-1,1,1,1), the future-directed coordinate field, global inertial charts, translations, displacements and the coordinate cone sets; the lemma proves the coordinate criterion and closure under sums for it.

contents.name: Section 1.11 printed pp. 15-16: the closed future cone in inertial coordinates, with finite sums of future causal vectors staying in the cone and the strict timelike case
contents.support: The lemma proves that in every inertial chart a nonzero vector is future timelike/null/causal exactly when v^0>|v_s|, 0<v^0=|v_s|, v^0>=|v_s|, that the future cone and its closure are the coordinate cones, and that the future cone is closed under sums.

contents.name: Section 1.12 printed pp. 17-18, Definition 1.22 and Theorem 1.23 printed p. 19, section 4.4 printed pp. 137-141: isotone, semi-time, time and temporal functions; stable causality
contents.support: The implication from a past-timelike gradient to a time function and the exclusion of closed causal curves are proved locally from the absolutely continuous calculus; the source's equivalence theory is not assumed.

contents.name: Definition 2.16 and Lemma 2.17 printed pp. 33-34 and section 2.11 printed pp. 45-49: inextendibility and limit curve theorems
contents.support: The convergent-end extension and the normalized-geodesic ODE argument replace the limit-curve machinery with an explicit compact-graph ODE continuation proof.

contents.name: Sections 2.14-2.15 printed pp. 59-66 with Definition 2.19 printed p. 34 and Definition 2.95 printed p. 63: achronal and acausal sets; acausality strictly stronger
contents.support: The two-point null-separated witness realises exactly the strictness the source records.

contents.name: Sections 3.1-3.3 printed pp. 83-103 with Definition 3.14 printed p. 87 and Definition 3.35 printed p. 95: Cauchy sets, domains of dependence and Cauchy horizons
contents.support: The parameter-counting definition of a Cauchy set, achronality/acausality and the domains of dependence and Cauchy horizons are restated; no equivalence with global hyperbolicity is imported.

contents.name: Definition 1.34 printed p. 24 and sections 4.2-4.5 printed pp. 111-148 with Definition 4.117 printed p. 146: the causal ladder and global hyperbolicity
contents.support: The chosen formulation (strong causality plus compact causal diamonds) is exactly the traditional formulation recorded by the source; the equivalent Cauchy-existence characterisation is explicitly not used or asserted.

contents.name: Definition 4.117 and Theorem 4.119 printed pp. 146-147, with the Minkowski model of section 1.1 printed pp. 3-6
contents.support: Minkowski global hyperbolicity is proved directly from the explicit cone and compactness computations rather than by quoting the general characterisation.

contents.name: Sections 4.2-4.3 printed pp. 111-137 with Proposition 4.18 and Definition 4.19 printed p. 113: closed timelike curves, vicious and totally vicious spacetimes
contents.support: The translation-quotient countermodel is proved as an explicit total-viciousness and no-Cauchy-set theorem.

contents.name: Sections 6.2-6.3 printed pp. 161-169: the Riccati and Raychaudhuri equations (6.4)-(6.6) for the Weingarten map and the focusing arguments
contents.support: The Raychaudhuri equation and the finite-time focusing bound are derived for the timelike geodesic congruence of this library with the metric-selected connection.

contents.name: Sections 6.5-6.6.1 printed pp. 171-179: global focusing, completeness, and the existence of singularities as closed trapped sets
contents.reason: A singularity theorem needs its own energy, causality and compactness hypotheses and a complete proof; the page proves only the local focusing bound and records the deferral in its scope remark.

contents.name: Sections 6.6.2-6.6.4 printed pp. 179-192: the Penrose, Hawking-Penrose and Hawking singularity theorems
contents.reason: Global singularity theorems are not part of this page's claim inventory and are deferred to the later pages of the track; no such theorem is used or cited as established.

sources.title: E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035 (2007)
sources.locator: Chapter 2 printed pp. 15-38 (hypersurfaces, induced metric, unit normal, extrinsic curvature, Gauss-Codazzi); section 3.2.1 printed p. 39 (Cauchy surfaces and global hyperbolicity); sections 4.1-4.2 printed pp. 51-59 (projection of the Einstein equation) and section 4.4.3 printed p. 64 (Hamiltonian and momentum constraint equations)

contents.name: Sections 2.3-2.4 printed pp. 19-34: induced metric, unit normal n.n = -1, extrinsic curvature K = -gamma*grad n, sphere and plane examples
contents.support: The construction of the future unit normal, the induced metric and the symmetric second fundamental form is proved locally; the source's sign convention is recorded as the negative of the library convention and consumers are directed to the library definition.

contents.name: Sections 2.4-2.5 printed pp. 28-39: spacelike hypersurfaces, Gauss, Codazzi and Ricci relations
contents.reason: The equivalent constraint form in terms of the induced scalar curvature and the divergence of K requires the Gauss-Codazzi relations and is deferred to the PDE treatment; this page keeps the projection form and says so.

contents.name: Section 3.2.1 p. 39: Cauchy surface met once and only once; global hyperbolicity definitions
contents.support: The Cauchy-set definition is adopted in parameter-counting form; the source's equivalence to the existence of a Cauchy surface is not asserted.

contents.name: Sections 4.1-4.2 printed pp. 51-59 and section 4.4.3 printed p. 64: projections of the Einstein equation and the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints
contents.support: The normal and normal-tangential projections of the field equation are evaluated explicitly; the source's component (3+1) forms are the deferred Gauss-Codazzi rewriting.

contents.name: Section 2.2.3 printed pp. 18-19: the curvature tensor of the Levi-Civita connection
contents.support: The lemma proves that a chart with constant components has vanishing metric-selected Christoffel symbols and curvature by uniqueness of the torsion-free metric-compatible connection; the source supplies the curvature convention only.

sources.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), 125 PDF pages
sources.locator: Section 10.2 printed p. 119 (PDF p. 120) extrinsic curvature, independence of the extension, projection formula (10.2); section 10.4 printed p. 123 (PDF p. 124) initial data (Sigma, h, K) and the constraints; section 10.5 printed pp. 123-124 (PDF pp. 124-125) the initial value problem, domain of dependence and maximal Cauchy development

contents.name: Section 10.2 p. 119: extrinsic curvature, its independence of the extension of n and the projection formula (10.2)
contents.support: The independence of the extension and the projection formula are proved; only the sign differs between the source's signature and the library convention, and that is stated.

contents.name: Section 10.4 p. 123: initial data (Sigma, h, K) and the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints
contents.support: The data and constraint equations are defined in projection form, with the equivalent component form and the existence theory deferred.

contents.name: Section 10.5 pp. 123-124: the initial value problem, domain of dependence and maximal Cauchy development
contents.reason: The existence and uniqueness of developments and the maximal development require the local Einstein-matter well-posedness theory and global gluing; this page defines maximality and asserts neither existence nor uniqueness. Censorship is not used.

contents.name: Section 2.1 printed p. 25 (PDF p. 26): the Minkowski metric eta_{mu nu} = diag(-1,1,1,1) on R^4
contents.support: Independent confirmation of the constant Lorentz form on R^4 with signature (-,+,+,+); the definition states the field eta and verifies its inertia from the constant component matrix.

sources.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), 238 PDF pages
sources.locator: Ch. 1 printed p. 7 (PDF p. 14) light cones and the timelike/null/spacelike classification; Ch. 4 printed pp. 117-127 (PDF pp. 124-134) the weak energy condition, the initial value problem, domains of dependence, Cauchy horizons and the Misner-space warning; Ch. 3 printed pp. 75-76 (PDF pp. 82-83) the commutator of covariant derivatives (3.65)-(3.66) and the Riemann tensor (3.67)

contents.name: Ch. 4 pp. 125-127: the initial value formulation, domains of dependence, Cauchy horizons and the Misner-space warning
contents.support: The warning is realised as a proved translation-quotient theorem with a closed future timelike curve and no Cauchy set.

contents.name: Ch. 4 p. 117: the energy-momentum tensor and the weak energy condition (4.72)
contents.support: The weak energy condition supplies the physical motivation for the geometric hypothesis Ric >= 0 in the focusing statement; the theorem itself takes that sign as an explicit geometric hypothesis and asserts no energy condition.

contents.name: Ch. 1 p. 7: null-separated events inside the light cone structure
contents.support: The null-separated pair of events is the concrete witness.

contents.name: Ch. 3 pp. 75-76: the commutator of covariant derivatives (3.65)-(3.66) and the Riemann tensor (3.67)
contents.support: The component identity is proved in a point-normal chart in the sign conventions of this library.

contents.name: Ch. 1 printed pp. 5-7 (PDF pp. 12-14): the light-cone structure and the timelike/null/spacelike classification of displacements
contents.support: Used as an independent treatment of the cone criterion that the local lemma proves in full in inertial coordinates; the empty interior of the cone and the strictness of the timelike inequality are absorbed in the lemma's step 5.2 and in the model definition of the cone sets.

contents.support: The radial congruence is computed explicitly; theta = -3/rho, sigma = omega = 0, and equality holds in the focusing bound.

contents.name: Sections 3.1-3.3 printed pp. 83-103 and section 4.5.4 printed pp. 146-148: Cauchy hypersurfaces and global hyperbolicity
contents.support: The vertical geodesics of the slab realise the finite-parameter boundary approach in a globally hyperbolic model.
